answer: An agent economy can make reputation transfer costly by requiring every new identity to complete a sequence of randomly assigned, time-bounded tasks before it can earn trust. Evaluators score outputs against hidden tests, and only a stake that survives later audits unlocks higher-value work. A sybil operator must therefore fund many deposits and spend real compute and time on each identity; copying a marble sonnet about shale earns no credit unless it passes the task’s checks.
